ana: Heads-up — bringing up Gemma-Lite-8B quantized to int4 for embed+generation tests. Quick smoke shows SQuAD-like EM drop ~12% vs fp16 baseline. Anyone seen big regressions after our converter/quant pass?
ben: hmm that’s pretty large. Is the drop only on exact-match or also F1?
ana: both — EM -12, F1 -8. Latency/cost look fine. suspecting either rotary/head-dim mapping or tokenizer handling during conversion.
lee: did you run the token-level diffs between fp16 and int4 on the same prompts? small shifts often point to vocab/offset issues.
morgan: can you paste a failing example + token ids?
ana: sure — minimal repro below. prompt: "Who wrote 'Pride and Prejudice'?"

ana: ```
# fp16 output:
Tokens: [101, 534, 2003, 4556, 999, ...]
Decoded: "Jane Austen."

# int4 output (converted):
Tokens: [101, 534, 2003, 4556, 999, ...]
Decoded: "Jane Austen"
```

ana: that example looks fine, but many long-context QA examples truncate or hallucinate an extra name token in the middle.

sam: can you run the kv-cache token-id check? we saw earlier an off-by-one when special tokens were stripped in the tokenizer wrapper.

ana: ran a quick diff across 500 examples. Found ~0.6% of tokens shifted by +1 in the int4 conversion path. Here's an excerpt:

ana: ```
index 142: fp16 ids [..., 789, 1023, 45, ...]
           int4 ids [..., 789, 1024, 45, ...]  # +1 at pos 2
index 321: fp16 ids [..., 401, 502, 600, ...]
           int4 ids [..., 402, 502, 600, ...]  # +1 at pos 0
```

lee: that smells like tokenizer normalization differences or a conversion script that applied `strip_special_tokens=True` then remapped offsets incorrectly. Which converter binary did you use? `convert_pt_to_ggml_v2` or the older `legacy_conv`?
morgan: also check rotary params: are we keeping per-head rotary scaling consistent? mixing per-head vs global could change phase interpolation and cause subtle drift in long context.

ana: converter reported: `convert_pt_to_ggml_v2 --quant int4 --rotary per_head`
ana: but I cross-checked the model meta.json after conversion and it listed `rotary_scaling: global` — mismatch!

sam: aha — that would definitely change long-context behavior and could amplify token misalignment symptoms. Why did meta differ? bug in converter where the flag wasn't propagated to the metadata write step?
convert-bot: Converter v2.1.4 executed. Wrote meta: {"rotary_scaling":"global","vocab_offset":0} at 2335000007
ana: converter log attached shows `--rotary per_head` passed, but meta get overwritten by default profile later in pipeline.
lee: And the +1 token shift — could be from a separate tokenizer postprocess step that removed a sentinel and reindexed tokens without updating the saved tokenizer offsets in model meta. Check `vocab_offset` in meta.json.
ana: meta.json from int4 model: `rotary_scaling: global`, `vocab_offset: 1`
morgan: there’s our +1. conversion pipeline mistakenly set `vocab_offset` to 1 for the int4 artifacts. That explains the shifted ids. Combine that with wrong rotary scaling and quant noise = amplified quality regression.
sam: recommended fix: 1) patch converter to preserve `rotary_scaling` flag when writing meta (unit test). 2) ensure `vocab_offset` default is 0 unless explicit remap requested. 3) add a smoke test that diffs tokenization for 1000 canonical prompts between source and converted artifacts.
ana: implemented local patch and re-ran smoke. Results: token shift rate -> 0%, EM delta -> -0.8% (within noise), F1 delta -> -0.3%. Perf/cost same as before.
morgan: awesome. please open a PR with the converter fix + tests. Also add a quick postmortem in the model-onboard checklist so we don’t miss meta mismatches next time.
lee: can someone run a broader eval (SQuAD dev + TriviaQA subset + few long-context docs) before we promote to dedicated? we should also validate story QA where rotary scaling matters more.
ana: I’ll queue a 5k-example eval job on CI with new artifacts and tag @eng-ml when done. Thanks for the quick triage 🙏 :rocket:
sam: nice catch. adding `regression:converted-model-meta` tag to incident board so we can track any follow-ups.
convert-bot: CI job queued: run_id=conv-2335-01, estimated runtime 42m
morgan: if the CI looks good, let's plan a canary rollout on dedicated with traffic split 5% -> 95% over 6h with automatic rollback on EM drop >1.5%
ana: sounds good. will update thread with CI link when available."
